re_line: Nvidia-China spy scandal widens · Taiwan balloons ahead of Nov 28 vote · Beijing cuts margin rule amid rout · Dutch FM in Beijing
morning_memo: WSJ identifies Li Ming, a business associate of Alice Huang, as the figure behind Megaspeed's bulk Nvidia chip purchases funneled toward China, deepening the espionage scandal tied to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair.
Taiwan's defense ministry recorded ten Chinese balloons over three days, plus 24 PLA aircraft and 11 warships around the island, five days before the Nov. 28 local elections.

Chinese exchanges cut the minimum margin-trading requirement to 80 percent from 100 percent effective Nov. 30 as state funds pushed ETF buying to a record to arrest a selloff that drove the Hang Seng down 5.77% today.

key_stat.label: Chinese balloons detected over Taiwan in three days
key_stat.context: Taiwan's defense ministry logged the balloons alongside 24 PLA aircraft and 11 warships five days before the Nov. 28 local elections; it recorded 57 balloons around the Jan. 2024 presidential vote.

prc_government.action: PBOC conducts 499.5 billion yuan overnight reverse repo as rate anchor shifts
prc_government.detail: The PBOC's policy rate switched from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate on Nov. 2; Q3 DR001 averaged 1.38% and fell to roughly 1.25% after the switch, per the report.

prc_government.ministry: NDRC, Ministry of Civil Affairs, NHC, Ministry of Education
prc_government.ministry_chinese: 国家发展改革委、民政部、国家卫健委、教育部
prc_government.action: China sets 2030 targets for elderly and childcare support
prc_government.document: 'One Old, One Young' Service System Construction Implementation Plan
prc_government.detail: The plan sets 2030 targets to expand elder care and childcare services nationwide, including encouraging AI companions and service robots for elder-care settings, per Reuters.

prc_government.action: Customs issues decision amending customs regulations
prc_government.document: 海关总署关于修改部分规章的决定
prc_government.detail: The General Administration of Customs published an order amending certain existing customs regulations, per a MOFCOM-hosted notice.

calendar_watch.headline: Taiwan nine-in-one local elections
calendar_watch.detail: Voters choose 22 mayors and magistrates plus roughly 11,000 local offices, read as a mid-term on President Lai Ching-te; PLA balloon and aircraft activity has intensified beforehand.

calendar_watch.headline: Dutch FM Berendsen's first China visit concludes
calendar_watch.detail: Dutch Foreign Minister Berendsen visits China Nov. 23-25 at the invitation of Wang Yi, his first trip since taking office.

calendar_watch.headline: Interpol 94th General Assembly opens in Hong Kong
calendar_watch.detail: Hong Kong hosts the assembly Nov. 30-Dec. 3 with citywide drone, harbour and road restrictions in force.

calendar_watch.headline: Nanjing Massacre National Memorial Day
calendar_watch.detail: China's annual state commemoration of the 1937 Nanjing Massacre.

calendar_watch.headline: G20 Leaders' Summit opens in Doral, Miami
calendar_watch.detail: The US hosts the G20 summit Dec. 14-15; Xi Jinping's attendance has not been confirmed.

overnight_items.headline: China Sentences Official to Death for Spying for Foreign Power
overnight_items.body_text: Bloomberg reports a Chinese official was sentenced to death for spying for a foreign power under state-secret-protection and espionage laws. The case adds to a string of recent counterintelligence prosecutions as Beijing tightens state-security enforcement.

overnight_items.headline: Taiwan Risk Could Hit Apple, Nvidia Stocks, Fund Manager Warns
overnight_items.body_text: Jupiter Asset Management's Sam Konrad told CNBC that Taiwan geopolitical risk is partly priced into Taiwanese tech stocks but not fully into US tech names. He said Apple and Nvidia are entirely reliant on Taiwan's chip supply chain.

overnight_items.headline: Hong Kong Imposes Drone, Harbour and Road Curbs for Interpol Assembly
overnight_items.body_text: Hong Kong will enforce air, sea and land restrictions including a drone ban and Victoria Harbour marine traffic limits during Interpol's 94th General Assembly, running Nov. 30 to Dec. 3. The curbs mark one of the city's largest security operations for an international gathering this year.

overnight_items.headline: Beijing Hails 'Healthy Competition' After Hong Kong Election Committee Vote
overnight_items.body_text: The Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office praised record turnout in Sunday's small-circle Election Committee race, which selects the body choosing Hong Kong's chief executive. Several heavyweight candidates suffered surprise losses.

overnight_items.headline: Crypto Exchange Collapse Hits Chinese Investors Hunting for Yield
overnight_items.body_text: Nikkei Asia reports mainland Chinese investors were caught up in a crypto exchange collapse after placing funds in a stablecoin product in July. The case shows continued capital flows from China into offshore crypto despite domestic restrictions.

overnight_items.headline: Taiwanese Banks Deploy AI to Counter Rising Cyberattacks
overnight_items.body_text: Taiwan Cooperative Bank and First Commercial Bank told CNA that suspicious probes roughly doubled this year, with First Commercial's firewall blocking about 2.2 million attacks from January through October. Banks are deploying AI-powered detection tools though none confirmed autonomous-AI-driven attacks.

overnight_items.headline: Premier Cho Accuses Taoyuan Mayor of Delaying TSMC Project
overnight_items.body_text: Taiwan News reports Premier Cho Jung-tai accused Taoyuan Mayor Chang Shan-cheng of delaying a TSMC project in the city. The dispute surfaces days before Taiwan's Nov. 28 local elections, in which Taoyuan's mayorship is contested.

overnight_items.headline: Hong Kong Films on Pro-Democracy Movement Win at Taiwan's Golden Horse Awards
overnight_items.body_text: AFP reports Hong Kong films inspired by the city's pro-democracy movement won awards at Taiwan's Golden Horse Awards, with one acceptance speech dedicated to 'those in prison.' The win highlights Taiwan as a platform for Hong Kong-themed work no longer screened at home.

overnight_items.headline: China Is Getting Inflation 'in All the Wrong Places,' Japan Times Says
overnight_items.body_text: A Japan Times commentary argues China's inflation pressures are emerging in the wrong parts of the economy even as consumer prices stay soft. The piece follows October data showing producer prices at a multi-year high alongside weak consumer inflation.

overnight_items.headline: China's Steel Sector Bifurcates as Iron Ore Demand Stays Robust
overnight_items.body_text: A Reuters commentary describes a widening split within China's steel industry even as iron ore demand remains resilient. The divergence points to uneven capacity utilization across mills amid ongoing overcapacity concerns.

us_china.headline: WaPo Traces Nvidia's Years-Long Washington Campaign to Keep Selling Chips to China
us_china.body_text: The Washington Post details how Nvidia lobbied Washington for years to preserve access to China for its advanced chips, context for the current scandal over CEO Jensen Huang's ties to suspected intelligence contact Alice Huang. The piece traces policy fights predating Megaspeed's chip acquisitions now under investigation.

us_china.headline: Senator Kennedy Presses for Scrutiny of Lutnick Over China's Chip Access
us_china.body_text: Sen. Kennedy is urging scrutiny of Commerce Secretary **Howard Lutnick** over how China obtained access to Nvidia's advanced chips, the Washington Post reports. The push adds Senate pressure to the inquiry already underway into the Megaspeed-Alice Huang affair.

us_china.headline: NYT: Alice Huang Stayed in Contact With China's Spy Agency During Nvidia CEO Affair
us_china.body_text: The New York Times reports **Alice Huang** remained in contact with officials from China's Ministry of State Security throughout her affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, per Reuters' summary. The contact period overlapped at least partly with Megaspeed's large-scale Nvidia chip purchases.

us_china.headline: CNN: Suspected Chinese Agents Used Fake Job Listings to Target US Officials
us_china.body_text: CNN reports suspected Chinese intelligence operatives built a web of fake companies advertising jobs to lure current and former US officials into divulging government secrets. The scheme is described as more pervasive than previously known, adding a new vector to the espionage picture surfacing alongside the Nvidia-Megaspeed case.

us_china.headline: Caixin: New US Rules Tighten Overseas Foundry Access for Chinese Chip Firms
us_china.body_text: Caixin reports new US regulations are closing off channels Chinese chip companies had used to fabricate designs at offshore foundries. The rules add to export-control pressure building after the Megaspeed chip-diversion revelations.

us_china.headline: Trump Weighs Curbs on US Firms Building Data Centers Overseas, Tariff Threat
us_china.body_text: Caixin reports the Trump administration is considering restrictions on US companies building data centers abroad, threatening high tariffs on firms that do so. The move follows scrutiny of how US-made AI chips have ended up inside China via offshore computing arrangements.

us_china.headline: FAI Analyst: 'Very Good Chance' Nvidia Knew of Chips' Military End Use in China
us_china.body_text: Former State Department official **Ryan Fedasiuk**, now at FAI, told CNBC there is a strong likelihood Nvidia knew of potential military or intelligence end-users accessing its chips in China. He said congressional scrutiny of Nvidia now extends well beyond the allegations surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's affair.

china_world.headline: Taiwan's MAC: China's Ethnic Unity Law Escalates 'Legal Warfare' Against Taiwan
china_world.body_text: Mainland Affairs Council Minister **Chiu Chui-cheng** said China's Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law, in force since July 1, disguises unification as ethnic unity and escalates Beijing's legal warfare from 'opposing independence' to 'forcing unification.' He called it part of a long-arm jurisdiction network built over recent years.

china_world.headline: Departing Japanese Envoy to Taiwan Bids Farewell: 'Long Live Japan-Taiwan Friendship'
china_world.body_text: Japan's outgoing representative to Taiwan, Katayama, delivered a farewell address titled 'Long live Japan-Taiwan friendship' as the envoy's term concludes, Focus Taiwan reports. No further details on a successor were given.

china_world.headline: China, Switzerland Hold Fifth Round of FM-Level Strategic Dialogue
china_world.body_text: China's foreign ministry announced the fifth round of the China-Switzerland foreign minister-level strategic dialogue on Nov. 23. A separate MOFA announcement said Swiss Vice President and Foreign Minister Cassis will visit China.

china_world.headline: China to Cut Tariffs on Canadian Pork, Seafood After Xi-Carney APEC Meeting
china_world.body_text: Per DW Chinese reporting on the Nov. 17 Xi-Carney meeting on the sidelines of the Shenzhen APEC summit, China will lower tariffs on Canadian pork and seafood exports. In exchange, Canada agreed to extend existing relief on certain Chinese steel and aluminum tariffs by two years.

china_world.headline: China-Mongolia-Russia Passenger Rail Service to Run Weekly Starting Nov. 25
china_world.body_text: China's state railway operator will run the Beijing-Ulaanbaatar-Irkutsk international passenger train weekly in both directions starting Nov. 25, MOFCOM announced. The 2,666-kilometer route takes 55 hours and crosses border posts at Erenhot, Zamyn-Üüd, Sükhbaatar and Naushki.

china_world.headline: CSRC Chairman Wu Qing Meets Indian Ambassador on Capital Markets Cooperation
china_world.body_text: China Securities Regulatory Commission Chairman **Wu Qing** met Indian Ambassador to China Vikram Kumar Doraiswami in Beijing on Nov. 23 to discuss global financial market conditions and China-India capital markets cooperation, per Yicai. No specific agreements were announced.

top_stories.headline: WSJ Names Megaspeed Associate Li Ming in Nvidia-China Chip Funneling Probe
top_stories.body: The Wall Street Journal identifies **Li Ming** as the business associate of **Alice Huang** accused of directing Megaspeed's large-scale purchases of Nvidia chips destined for China. The report ties Li Ming's activities to the broader espionage scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Huang, who US officials say was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security during the relationship.

top_stories.headline: Taiwan Detects 10 Chinese Balloons in Three Days Ahead of Local Elections
top_stories.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded two more Chinese balloons crossing into its airspace in the 24 hours to 6am Sunday, bringing the three-day total to *10*, five days before the Nov. 28 nine-in-one local elections. The ministry also tracked 24 PLA aircraft, 11 warships and one official ship, with 17 aircraft crossing the Taiwan Strait median line into Taiwan's air defense identification zone.

top_stories.headline: China Cuts Stock Margin Requirement to 80% as State Funds Buy Record ETFs
top_stories.body: Chinese exchanges will lower the minimum margin-trading requirement to *80 percent* from 100 percent starting Nov. 30, Bloomberg reports. The step follows a deepening selloff that pushed the Hang Seng down 5.77% and the SSE Composite down 1.27% today, with state-backed funds ramping ETF purchases to a record to cushion the rout.

top_stories.headline: DNI Confirms Beijing Obtained Access to Advanced US AI Chips
top_stories.body: Director of National Intelligence **Jay Clayton**, per CNN, told Dana Bash that China gained access to advanced US AI chips, addressing fallout from the Nvidia espionage scandal. The confirmation comes as Congress presses Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over export-control enforcement following revelations about Megaspeed's chip acquisitions.

top_stories.headline: NYT: Chinese Military Researchers Fear AI Makes Nuclear Forces More Vulnerable
top_stories.body: The New York Times reports Chinese military researchers are studying how to harness artificial intelligence while worrying the technology leaves China's nuclear forces more vulnerable to attack. The reporting follows the Nov. 19 Shenzhen trilateral declaration between **Xi Jinping**, Trump and Putin that included language on reducing nuclear risk.

top_stories.headline: Bloomberg Explainer: What's at Stake in Taiwan's Nov. 28 Local Elections
top_stories.body: Bloomberg outlines the stakes in Taiwan's Nov. 28 nine-in-one elections for 22 mayors, magistrates and roughly 11,000 local offices, framed as a midterm referendum on President **Lai Ching-te**. The piece notes Beijing's heightened attention to the vote amid the balloon and PLA activity reported this week.

also_today.headline: FT: Xi Needs Trump More Than Ever After Shenzhen Summit
also_today.body_text: FT says the Shenzhen summit shows high stakes for Beijing as Washington voices grow for tougher China measures.

also_today.headline: Bloomberg: A 'Vibecoder' Boomtown Signals Shifts in China's Economy
also_today.body_text: Bloomberg profiles a Chinese town full of AI 'vibecoders' as a window into the economy's tech-driven transformation.

also_today.headline: China's Next AI Deals Clouded by Post-Anthropic-IPO Selloff
also_today.body_text: Bloomberg reports the selloff following Anthropic's IPO is complicating valuations for China's upcoming AI financing deals.

also_today.headline: Former Zhejiang Official Given Suspended Death Sentence for Bribery
also_today.body_text: A Jiangxi court sentenced ex-Zhejiang NPC deputy director Gao Xingfu to a suspended death sentence for bribes exceeding 193 million yuan.

also_today.headline: MOFCOM Responds to US FCC's Proposed Curbs on Chinese Telecom Carriers
also_today.body_text: China's commerce ministry fielded questions on an FCC proposal barring Chinese carriers from directly obtaining US VoIP phone numbers.

also_today.headline: VOA: Taiwan Election Campaigns Center on Governance, Not Unification
also_today.body_text: VOA Chinese reports Taiwan's local election campaigns focus on municipal governance and swing voters, with unification-independence themes receding.

also_today.headline: Chinese Automakers Now Outsell Japanese Rivals in 39 Markets
also_today.body_text: Nikkei reports Chinese brands have overtaken Japanese competitors' new-vehicle market share in 39 countries, led by EV sales.

also_today.headline: Two Taiwanese Dignitaries Attend Japan's Shuri Castle Restoration Ceremony
also_today.body_text: Focus Taiwan reports two Taiwanese officials attended the restoration ceremony for Japan's Shuri Castle.

also_today.headline: Taiwan Scholar: Can the US Close China's Path to Advanced AI Chips?
also_today.body_text: RFI Chinese interviews Taiwan scholar Kenny Chang on whether Washington can block China's access to advanced AI computing after the Nvidia affair.

also_today.headline: Japan Island Resident Near Taiwan Fears War as China Ties Sour
also_today.body_text: Kyodo reports residents of a Japanese island near Taiwan voice fear of conflict amid deteriorating China-Japan relations.

business_economy.headline: China's State Funds Push ETF Buying to Record as Market Rout Deepens
business_economy.body_text: Bloomberg reports China's state-backed 'national team' funds ramped ETF purchases to a record level as the selloff deepens, with the Hang Seng down 5.77% and the SSE Composite down 1.27% today.

business_economy.headline: Gold Imports Keep China's $1 Trillion Trade Surplus in Check
business_economy.body_text: Bloomberg reports a surge in Chinese gold imports is offsetting export strength, holding China's trade surplus near the $1 trillion mark rather than pushing it higher.

business_economy.headline: BYD Shares Fall After Dutch Court Bars Ti7 SUV Sales in EU
business_economy.body_text: BYD shares dropped after a Dutch court barred sales of its Ti7 SUV model across the EU, the Wall Street Journal reports.

business_economy.headline: Ant Group Bets on Simplexity to Compete in China's Humanoid Robot Race
business_economy.body_text: Bloomberg reports Ant Group is backing Simplexity as its vehicle to compete in China's humanoid robotics race, part of a broader wave of Chinese capital flowing into embodied-AI startups.

business_economy.headline: China's Electric Truck Boom Lifts Demand for Lithium
business_economy.body_text: Reuters reports China's fast-growing electric truck segment is driving new demand for lithium, adding a growth vector beyond passenger EVs for battery material suppliers.

business_economy.headline: FT: China Is Winning the Car War as Western Carmakers Retreat
business_economy.body_text: The Financial Times reports Western carmakers have been routed from the China market as EVs go mainstream, and are now fighting to avoid a similar fate in their home markets.

business_economy.headline: World's First Offshore Yuan Bond ETF Lists in Hong Kong
business_economy.body_text: Caixin reports the world's first offshore renminbi ('dim sum') bond ETF listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange Nov. 23, tracking the Bloomberg Offshore RMB Index; offshore yuan bond issuance has surpassed Chinese-dollar bond issuance for the first time this year.

official_line.speaker: People's Bank of China
official_line.topic: Monetary policy stance and rate-anchor shift
official_line.statement: We will continue to implement a moderately loose monetary policy, creating a suitable monetary and financial environment for stable economic growth, high-quality development, and smooth operation of financial markets.
official_line.original_zh: 坚持实施好适度宽松的货币政策，为经济稳定增长、高质量发展和金融市场平稳运行营造适宜的货币金融环境。
official_line.context: The report was released after the PBOC shifted its policy rate anchor from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate on Nov. 2.
official_line.source: PBOC Q3 Monetary Policy Report, via Sohu

official_line.speaker: Guo Jiakun
official_line.topic: Poland PM Tusk's reported December China visit
official_line.statement: High-level exchanges play an important role in developing China-Poland relations. Regarding the visit you mentioned, I currently have no information to provide.
official_line.original_zh: 高层交往对中波关系的发展具有重要作用。关于你提到的访问，我目前没有可以提供的信息。
official_line.context: A Polish news agency asked whether PM Donald Tusk would visit China in December amid EU-China trade friction and the Ukraine war.

official_line.speaker: Guo Jiakun
official_line.statement: China has always believed that dialogue and negotiation are the only viable way to resolve the Ukraine crisis.
official_line.original_zh: 中方始终认为对话谈判是解决乌克兰危机唯一可行出路
official_line.context: Reporters asked whether the Ukraine crisis was discussed at the Nov. 19 Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting in Shenzhen.

official_line.speaker: Guo Jiakun
official_line.statement: Per Xinhua: At the invitation of Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Dutch Foreign Minister Berendsen will visit China from November 23 to 25.
official_line.original_zh: 应中共中央政治局委员、外交部长王毅邀请，荷兰外交大臣贝伦德森将于11月23日至25日访华。
official_line.context: The announcement comes as Berendsen makes his first visit to China since taking office as Dutch foreign minister.

personnel_changes.position: Director, Gansu Provincial State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission
personnel_changes.name: Cheng Zijian (程子建)
personnel_changes.detail: Cheng Zijian was named director of Gansu's SASAC, per China Economic Daily.
